target: Dywedodd Siân ei bod hi'n mynd i Gaerdydd yfory.
english: Siân said she was going to Cardiff tomorrow.
tip: For she in reported speech use ‘ei bod hi’: ‘dywedodd Siân ei bod hi'n mynd’ = Siân said she was going.

target: Dywedodd fy ffrind ei fod e'n symud i Lundain.
english: My friend said he was moving to London.
tip: For he in reported speech use ‘ei fod e’: ‘ei fod e'n symud’ = that he was moving.

target: Mae straeon gwerin yn cael eu hadrodd.
english: Folk stories are told.
tip: ‘cael’ plus a possessive forms the passive: ‘yn cael eu hadrodd’ = are told, literally get their telling.

target: Mae brecwast wedi'i gynnwys.
english: Breakfast is included.
tip: In ‘wedi'i gynnwys’, ‘wedi’ plus ‘'i’ marks a passive: has been included, and the ‘'i’ soft-mutates the verb to ‘gynnwys’.

target: Mae angen ymbarél heddiw.
english: An umbrella is needed today.
tip: ‘mae angen ymbarél’ means an umbrella is needed. ‘mae angen’ plus a noun expresses a need, with no separate word for a.

target: Dwedodd hi ei bod hi wedi penderfynu.
english: She said she had decided.
tip: Reported speech uses ‘bod’, not the plain verb: ‘ei bod hi’ means that she, so ‘ei bod hi wedi penderfynu’ = that she had decided.

target: Mae cynllunio ymlaen llaw yn arbed amser ac arian.
english: Planning ahead saves time and money.
tip: And is normally ‘ac’ before a vowel and ‘a’ before a consonant. Here ‘amser ac arian’ = time and money, ‘ac’ because ‘arian’ starts with a vowel.

target: Gofynnodd e a oeddwn i wedi gorffen y llyfr eto.
english: He asked if I had finished the book yet.
tip: ‘a’ opens an indirect yes or no question: ‘a oeddwn i wedi gorffen’ = whether I had finished.

target: Mae eu cerddoriaeth yn dod â llawenydd i lawer o bobl.
english: Their music brings joy to many people.
tip: ‘dod â’ is literally come with and means to bring: ‘yn dod â llawenydd’ = bringing joy.

target: Y ci sy wedi bwyta'r cig!
english: It's the dog that has eaten the meat!
tip: Fronting the subject adds emphasis: ‘y ci sy wedi bwyta’ puts the dog first, and ‘sy’ means the one that has.

target: Roedd ei thalent yn amlwg o oedran ifanc.
english: Her talent was obvious from a young age.
tip: ‘ei’ meaning her aspirate-mutates a following t to th: ‘talent’ becomes ‘ei thalent’.

target: Ei gardd hi yw'r un hardda yn y stryd.
english: Her garden is the prettiest in the street.
tip: The superlative ends in ‘-a’ or ‘-af’: ‘hardda’ = prettiest, formed from ‘hardd’.

target: Casglodd y tîm ddata o dri chant o gyfranogwyr.
english: The team collected data from three hundred participants.
tip: ‘tri’, meaning three, aspirate-mutates the next word: ‘cant’ becomes ‘tri chant’.

target: Rydyn ni wedi ymweld â phob castell yng ngogledd Cymru.
english: We have visited every castle in north Wales.
tip: ‘yn’ before a place nasal-mutates it and itself becomes ‘yng’: ‘gogledd’ turns into ‘yng ngogledd’ for in the north.

target: Mae hi wedi peidio â smocio.
english: She's stopped smoking.
tip: ‘peidio â’ means to stop or cease doing something: ‘wedi peidio â smocio’ = has stopped smoking.

target: Mae'r sbectol yn gwella fy ngolwg.
english: The spectacles improve my sight.
tip: ‘fy’, meaning my, nasal-mutates the next word: ‘golwg’ becomes ‘fy ngolwg’.

target: Mae ei ymroddiad i'r gymuned yn rhyfeddol.
english: His dedication to the community is remarkable.
tip: ‘ei’ meaning his leaves a following vowel unchanged: ‘ei ymroddiad’ = his dedication.

target: Mae'r mwyngloddiau glo wedi cau ers degawdau.
english: The coal mines have been closed for decades.
tip: ‘ers’ marks how long something has held up to now: ‘ers degawdau’ = for decades.

target: Mae'r enfys ddwbl yn ymestyn dros y dyffryn.
english: The double rainbow stretches over the valley.
tip: A feminine noun soft-mutates the adjective after it: ‘dwbl’ becomes ‘ddwbl’ in ‘enfys ddwbl’, since ‘enfys’ is feminine.

target: Fy nod yw dod yn rhugl yn Gymraeg.
english: My goal is to become fluent in Welsh.
tip: After ‘yn’ meaning in, a language name soft-mutates: ‘Cymraeg’ becomes ‘yn Gymraeg’ = in Welsh.

target: Byddai wedi bod yn well pe baen ni wedi gadael yn gynharach.
english: It would have been better if we had left earlier.
tip: ‘pe baen ni’ means if we had and opens an unreal condition, pairing with ‘byddai’ for would have.

target: Dw i wedi pasio!
english: I've passed!
tip: ‘wedi’ before a verb marks the perfect: ‘dw i wedi pasio’ = I have passed. Replace ‘wedi’ with ‘yn’ for I am passing.

target: Oeddech chi wedi gorffen?
english: Had you finished?
tip: An ‘oedd’ form plus ‘wedi’ is the past perfect: ‘oeddech chi wedi gorffen?’ = Had you finished?, one step back from the plain past.

target: Mae'r wy wedi'i ferwi.
english: The egg is boiled.
tip: ‘wedi'i’ plus a softened verb says it has been done to the thing: ‘wedi'i ferwi’ (from ‘berwi’) = boiled.

target: Mae'r llythyrau wedi'u hanfon.
english: The letters have been sent.
tip: For plural things use ‘wedi'u’, adding h before a vowel: ‘wedi'u hanfon’ (from ‘anfon’) = have been sent.

target: Dw i wedi blino'n lân.
english: I'm completely tired.
tip: ‘'n lân’, literally clean, works as an intensifier meaning completely: ‘wedi blino'n lân’ = worn out.

target: Mae hi newydd gyrraedd adref.
english: She has just arrived home.
tip: ‘newydd’ plus a softened verb means just did: ‘newydd gyrraedd’ (from ‘cyrraedd’) = has just arrived. Use ‘wedi’ for the plain perfect.

target: Dw i wedi gweithio yma am bum mlynedd.
english: I've worked here for five years.
tip: Counting years uses ‘blynedd’, not ‘blwyddyn’, and it nasal-mutates to ‘mlynedd’ after five: ‘bum mlynedd’ = five years.

target: Byddai hi wedi bod yn braf mynd ar wyliau eleni.
english: It would have been nice to have gone on holiday this year.
tip: ‘byddai’ plus ‘wedi bod’ is would have been: ‘byddai hi wedi bod yn braf’ = it would have been nice.

target: Rydyn ni wedi byw yn y pentref yma ers pymtheng mlynedd.
english: We have lived in this village for fifteen years.
tip: ‘ers’ covers a span still going: ‘wedi byw ... ers pymtheng mlynedd’ = have lived for fifteen years and still do.
